ArchitectureNotes.objective: Provide a GitHub-first, collection-led frontend task knowledge base whose target ConciseStudentTaskCards copy into fixed online-editor profiles without collection, verification, or graph drift.
ArchitectureNotes.non-goal: Do not build an executable learning platform, catalog generator, or mandatory repository runtime.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-1: Card title and metadata, thematic and interview collections, editor links, verification facts, and graph facts have different owners, so every affected surface must change atomically.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-2: Markdown review cannot prove execution in every student environment; local deterministic Markdown, collection, XML, and Beads synchronization checks are the publication gates, while final complete-library user acceptance gates only top-level story closure.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-3: Collapsed details prevent accidental spoilers but do not conceal solutions from raw Markdown or repository search.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-4: Publishing before deduplication can create several cards for the same learning goal.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-5: The concise target contract can be mistaken for completed migration while the current twenty cards still use legacy structure, so the exact compatibility inventory remains explicit until Phase 19.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-6: Real-work format, duration, thematic ownership, dedicated collection membership, and target-editor behavior can drift unless they cut over atomically.

contract.purpose: Define the repository's authoring, delivery, synchronization, verification, and stop-condition rules.

export-authoringRules.PURPOSE: Expose concise-card authoring, temporary legacy compatibility, delivery, tool-resolution, and synchronization requirements

export-verificationContracts.PURPOSE: Expose module, flow, Phase 16 through 20, and matching gate evidence without inferring future implementation

observability.evidence-anchor: M-GOVERNANCE / V-M-GOVERNANCE / XML roots and cross-references
observability.critical-check: All shared artifacts are valid and mutually consistent.

notes.note-1: The initial governance and Phases 8 through 15 of the approved student redesign are implemented; the published GitHub-rendered audit passed before final user acceptance.
notes.note-2: Phases 16 through 20 stage a new concise redesign; their planned state does not invalidate the historical Phase 8 through 15 evidence or claim the current cards are concise.

contract.purpose: Define focused and real-work ConciseStudentTaskCard structures for copy-ready self-contained frontend tasks.

type-TaskMetadata.PURPOSE: Exact five fields and controlled values for technology, thematic collection, one of five formats, difficulty, and integer duration

type-ConciseStudentTaskCard.PURPOSE: Title, target-editor instruction, visible condition, one technology-dependent minimal starter or minimum HTML fragment plus JavaScript, three closed hints, concise solution, and closed five-field metadata; multi-file is real-work only and every included changed solution file is complete with its matching starter FILE path

type-TaskClass.PURPOSE: Focused one-action 10–30 minute card or sequential real-work 45–60 minute card

type-EditorProfile.PURPOSE: Programiz, CodePen, TypeScript Playground, or React TypeScript copy-run contract

export-taskSchema.PURPOSE: Expose focused and real-work concise orders, minimal-code and FILE rules, progressive disclosure, solution boundaries, and metadata

observability.evidence-anchor: editor instruction; Условие; three exact hint summaries; Решение; О задаче
observability.critical-check: The selected task-class order and technology-dependent fences are exact, code is minimal and copy-ready, JavaScript has no full-document wrapper, real-work starter files are complete, every included changed solution file is complete with its matching starter FILE path, and every details block is closed by default.

notes.note-1: The template may contain fenced examples but introduces no runnable repository tooling.

contract.purpose: Deduplicate candidates and validate new or migrated cards for student structure, source-contract preservation, content, and local Markdown, collection, XML, and Beads synchronization.

type-CandidateRegister.PURPOSE: Finite Beads inventory with stable candidate IDs and terminal-decision accounting

type-CardMigrationEvidence.PURPOSE: Exactly slug, mode, editorProfile, sourceLearningGoal, sourcePrerequisite, sourceRuntimeAssumption, destinationLocations, targetEditorExpectedResult, targetEditorActualResult, and verdict in the matching card Beads issue; both targetEditor fields equal NOT_RUN: Markdown-only delivery

export-validateCandidate.PURPOSE: Apply identity, task-class, ConciseStudentTaskCard, local-completeness, preservation, structure, solution-content, and local Markdown, collection, XML, and Beads synchronization gates

const-legacyCompatibility.PURPOSE: Permit legacy structure only for the exact twenty pre-existing slugs until Phase 19, without granting concise migration PASS

target.source: docs/task-validation-policy.md; Beads validation and technical wave-publication records
target.tests: V-M-TASK-VALIDATION strict candidate and evidence checks

observability.evidence-anchor: validation decision; CardMigrationEvidence with both target-editor fields marked NOT_RUN; local deterministic verdict; collection sync; rejection or merge reason
observability.critical-check: Only accepted produces an AcceptedTaskCard; compatibility is not migration PASS; external editors, browsers, live APIs, and GitHub-rendered pages are not opened or operated for repository validation and their availability never determines PASS or BLOCKED.

notes.note-1: Temporary harnesses do not become a permanent repository runtime.
notes.note-2: External learning materials may supplement the card but cannot carry the local condition, text fixtures, starter code, solution, or required verification context.

contract.purpose: Store the current twenty legacy-compatible cards while migrating them in serialized waves to concise focused cards and adding one concise real-work card.

type-TaskMetadataSet.PURPOSE: Collection of five-field task metadata records exposed to thematic and interview collections

export-taskCard.PURPOSE: Expose one complete copy-ready task card through GitHub; Phase 19 requires all twenty-one exports to conform to ConciseStudentTaskCard

observability.evidence-anchor: task slug; selected mode; editor profile; five metadata values; preservation ledger; copy-ready code; local deterministic verdict; collection sync
observability.critical-check: A migrated card is locally complete, has exactly three progressive hints, contains no legacy markers or full-document JavaScript wrapper, records both target-editor result fields as NOT_RUN: Markdown-only delivery, passes local Markdown and synchronization checks, and resolves every required local media, collection, and supplementary link.

notes.note-1: A slug is stable. Renaming it is a migration that must verify every inbound reference.
notes.note-2: Collapsed solutions are spoiler-resistant, not access-controlled.
notes.note-3: The serialized wave Beads issue closes continuously after candidate recheck, local deterministic evidence, pushed commit, and the complete wave report pass.
notes.note-4: Each accepted task adds one export-<task-slug> public annotation under M-TASK-LIBRARY in the knowledge graph.
notes.note-5: Text code, HTML, test data, and scenarios remain inside the card; assets are reserved for media or other binary material that cannot reasonably be embedded.
notes.note-6: Phases 10 through 13 implemented all twenty existing card migrations; Phase 14 synchronized their final thematic and optional interview projections.
notes.note-7: The concise redesign is a new migration. The exact twenty legacy slugs remain a temporary compatibility state until their 8 + 8 + 4 focused migrations and the new users-api-list real-work card pass Phases 17 through 19.

contract.purpose: Provide the root student hub plus thematic, interview, and target real-work collection pages that lead students to task cards.

type-CollectionEntry.PURPOSE: Linked student title and exact integer duration copied from the card, plus one plain-language sentence only for thematic collections

export-studentIndex.PURPOSE: Expose the four-block root hub and, after Phase 19, ten thematic, three interview, and one real-work collection without duplicating card content

observability.evidence-anchor: root collection link; CollectionEntry; relative task link; student title; exact duration; unique thematic and optional interview membership
observability.critical-check: Every task appears in exactly one thematic collection and no more than one interview; only confirmed real-work cards additionally appear in the real-work collection; title, duration, format, links, and editor map agree with the card contract.

notes.note-1: The catalog is maintained by an AI agent under contract, not generated by a script.
notes.note-2: Phase 14 atomically replaced the old root task tables with the current four-block student hub after every collection and card passed.
notes.note-3: All ten thematic and three interview collection files are current student navigation; Phase 15 completed the published rendered audit.
notes.note-4: The four-block root still truthfully represents the implemented thirteen-page catalog. The fourteenth real-work page, twenty-first card, and root link remain planned until their atomic Phase 19 cutover.

DF-VALIDATE-TASK.NAME: ValidateTask
DF-VALIDATE-TASK.TRIGGER: Agent prepares a candidate for possible publication
DF-VALIDATE-TASK.step-1: The agent checks the learning goal against accepted tasks and merges semantically equivalent candidates.
DF-VALIDATE-TASK.step-2: The agent independently authors the candidate against the M-TASK-TEMPLATE ConciseStudentTaskCard contract.
DF-VALIDATE-TASK.step-3: The agent applies identity, task-class, concise-card, local-completeness, preservation, structure, solution-content, and local Markdown, collection, XML, and Beads synchronization gates.
DF-VALIDATE-TASK.step-4: The agent records both target-editor result fields as NOT_RUN: Markdown-only delivery and derives verdict only from local deterministic checks.
DF-VALIDATE-TASK.step-5: The agent records accepted, needs-rewrite, rejected, or duplicate in Beads; only accepted yields an AcceptedTaskCard.
DF-VALIDATE-TASK.evidence: Validation decision, CardMigrationEvidence when applicable, explicit NOT_RUN target-editor fields, local deterministic verdict, duplicate or rejection reason, thematic/interview/supported-real-work sync, and unresolved risk.

DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.NAME: PublishTaskWave
DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.TRIGGER: Eight to ten accepted task cards are ready
DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.step-1: The agent creates accepted task cards and optional colocated assets.
DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.step-2: The agent synchronizes exactly one thematic collection, zero or one interview collection, supported real-work membership when applicable, and one export-<task-slug> annotation per task.
DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.step-3: The agent runs V-M-TASK-LIBRARY, V-M-CATALOG, V-M-TASK-VALIDATION, and V-M-GOVERNANCE.
DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.step-4: The agent pushes the focused wave commit after all local deterministic checks pass.
DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.step-5: The agent publishes a complete wave report containing decisions, evidence, merges, checks, and remaining risks, then records the technical publication status.
DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.step-6: The agent closes the child Beads issue after every technical gate passes and continues to the next serialized wave without per-wave human approval.
DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.evidence: Accepted paths, thematic, optional interview and supported real-work CollectionEntry facts, graph annotations, validation or migration evidence, explicit NOT_RUN target-editor fields, local deterministic results, pushed commit, complete report, and wave technical-publication status.

DF-ADD-TASK.NAME: AddTask
DF-ADD-TASK.TRIGGER: Mentor asks an AI agent to add a task
DF-ADD-TASK.step-1: The agent reads M-GOVERNANCE, M-TASK-TEMPLATE, and M-TASK-VALIDATION.
DF-ADD-TASK.step-2: The agent resolves focused or real-work class, five metadata fields, exactly one thematic collection, optional interview and real-work membership, and one editor profile; ambiguity stops the change.
DF-ADD-TASK.step-4: An accepted card follows the same atomic card, thematic collection, optional interview, graph, verification, and Beads evidence contract as DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.
DF-ADD-TASK.step-5: The serialized wave Beads issue closes after its technical publication gates and complete report pass.
DF-ADD-TASK.evidence: Validation decision, task path, CollectionEntry, graph and verification entries, local link results, explicit NOT_RUN target-editor fields, local deterministic results, pushed commit, complete report, and technical publication status.

DF-STUDY-TASK.NAME: StudyTask
DF-STUDY-TASK.TRIGGER: Student opens the repository on GitHub
DF-STUDY-TASK.step-1: The student chooses a technology direction or interview from the root README.md student hub.
DF-STUDY-TASK.step-2: The student opens a collection and chooses a linked title using its plain-language description and exact duration.
DF-STUDY-TASK.step-3: The student opens the task, follows the named target-editor instruction, and copies the complete starter block or justified files.
DF-STUDY-TASK.step-4: The student attempts the visible condition and reveals the three hints one at a time only when needed.
DF-STUDY-TASK.step-5: The student opens the concise solution when needed, then uses browser Back to return to the same collection.
DF-STUDY-TASK.evidence: Working root-to-collection-to-card links, target-editor instruction, minimal copy-ready code, three closed hints, closed concise solution and metadata, matching title and duration, and browser Back behavior.

DF-UPDATE-TASK.NAME: UpdateTask
DF-UPDATE-TASK.TRIGGER: Agent changes or migrates task content, metadata, path, prerequisites, editor profile, or assets
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-1: The agent resolves the stable slug, source learning goal, source prerequisite, source runtime assumption, current thematic collection, optional interview, supported real-work membership when applicable, and editor profile.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-2: The agent selects the focused ConciseStudentTaskCard class for an existing card and records destination locations in CardMigrationEvidence before removing source information or text assets.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-3: The agent updates complete copy-ready code, records both target-editor fields as NOT_RUN: Markdown-only delivery, and reruns every affected local M-TASK-VALIDATION gate.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-4: The agent synchronizes exactly one thematic collection, zero or one interview, supported real-work membership when applicable, knowledge graph, verification plan, and Beads evidence.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-5: The agent checks title, duration, format, editor profile, thematic/interview/real-work membership uniqueness, multi-file completeness and FILE parity, assets, supplementary links, and relative links.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-6: A text asset is deleted only after the embedded replacement passes; a slug change uses a dedicated migration path and verifies all inbound references.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.evidence: CardMigrationEvidence, explicit NOT_RUN target-editor fields, local deterministic verdict, before/after student data, thematic, interview and supported real-work sync, resolved local links, graph delta, verification delta, and Beads record.

Phase-1.name: Governance
Phase-1.goal: Record approved requirements, worktree isolation, technology boundaries, module contracts, data flows, verification references, and stop conditions.
Phase-1.step-1: Finalize and review the written specification and all GRACE planning artifacts.

Phase-2.name: TaskContract
Phase-2.goal: Create the canonical GitHub-first task structure and strict validation policy before any task content is added.
Phase-2.step-2: Create docs/task-validation-policy.md and prove all terminal decisions and hybrid evidence routes.

Phase-3.name: StudentEntryPoint
Phase-3.goal: Create an understandable repository landing page and an explicit empty catalog state.
Phase-3.step-1: Create README.md with navigation rules and the catalog projection contract.

Phase-4.name: CandidateAudit
Phase-4.goal: Freeze a finite neutral Beads candidate register, deduplicate it, and record a validation decision for every stable candidate ID.
Phase-4.step-1: Freeze candidate IDs, apply DF-VALIDATE-TASK, and group accepted cards into waves of 8-10 with a permitted final wave of 1-7.

Phase-5.name: TaskWaves
Phase-5.goal: Publish strictly accepted tasks through serialized atomic task, catalog, graph, local deterministic evidence, pushed-commit, report, and technical-status updates.
Phase-5.step-1: Publish 8-10 accepted task cards from the canonical template, or 1-7 for the final incomplete wave.
Phase-5.step-2: Synchronize thematic student-catalog tables for the wave.
Phase-5.step-3: Apply graph and verification deltas, record the complete report and technical publication status in Beads, close the wave, and continue.

Phase-6.name: FinalAudit
Phase-6.goal: Prove that every candidate has a terminal decision and every accepted task remains unique, technically published, verified, and linked, then prepare the complete library for final user review.
Phase-6.step-1: Run full candidate-status, catalog, graph, XML, Markdown, link, branch-divergence, and technical publication checks; keep the top-level story open for final user acceptance.

Phase-7.name: ScaleReview
Phase-7.goal: Reassess controlled vocabularies and deterministic validation only after observed catalog size or drift justifies added tooling.
Phase-7.step-1: Review drift evidence and explicitly approve or reject automation.

Phase-8.name: StudentRedesignContract
Phase-8.goal: Implement the approved two-mode StudentTaskCard, five-field metadata, editor profiles, preservation evidence, collection ownership, and pending redesign roadmap.
Phase-8.step-1: Prove the local story checkout and synchronize authoring, template, validation, GRACE, and operational packet contracts without adding tooling.
Phase-8.step-2: Define both complete card modes, copy-ready and FILE rules, exact hints, metadata, and navigation.
Phase-8.step-3: Define CardMigrationEvidence, final target-editor evidence, preservation, content, synchronization, and rendered gates.

Phase-9.name: StudentCollections
Phase-9.goal: Create ten final thematic collection pages and three unlinked interview shells without changing the current root README.
Phase-9.step-1: Create the exact thirteen paths and verify thematic entries, interview-shell contract, links, titles, descriptions, and times.

Phase-10.name: JavaScriptDOMMigration
Phase-10.goal: Migrate the eight JavaScript and DOM cards and inline the stale-search text fixture.
Phase-10.step-1: Pass per-card preservation, structure, copy-run, target-editor, content, collection-sync, and asset-replacement evidence.

Phase-11.name: TypeScriptMigration
Phase-11.goal: Migrate four TypeScript cards while preserving exact TypeScript 5.9 behavior.
Phase-11.step-1: Pass per-card preservation, structure, TypeScript Playground, content, and collection-sync evidence.

Phase-12.name: HTMLCSSAccessibilityMigration
Phase-12.goal: Migrate four HTML, CSS, and accessibility cards and inline two text fixtures.
Phase-12.step-1: Pass CodePen, browser, manual visual, accessibility, content, collection-sync, and asset-replacement evidence.

Phase-13.name: ReactMigration
Phase-13.goal: Migrate four React TypeScript cards as complete src/App.tsx exercises with React 19.2 behavior.
Phase-13.step-1: Pass vite.new/react-ts copy-run, browser, lifecycle, content, and collection-sync evidence.

Phase-14.name: StudentHubCutover
Phase-14.goal: Populate three interviews, synchronize all twenty cards and thirteen collections, and atomically replace the root catalog with the four-block student hub.
Phase-14.step-1: Verify complete thematic and interview membership, exact duplicated fields, editor map, navigation, graph and verification sync, and root negative checks.

Phase-15.name: StudentRenderedAudit
Phase-15.goal: Audit the published root, thirteen collections, and twenty cards through complete URL inventory and deep GitHub-rendered student flows.
Phase-15.step-1: Record resolved URLs, visible titles, links, details behavior, every technology, interview, card mode, editor profile, former fixture card, and remaining risk before final user acceptance.

Phase-16.name: ConciseContractPreparation
Phase-16.goal: Stage the observable concise-card, compatibility, five-format, twenty-one-card, fourteen-collection, and deterministic cutover contracts without claiming any current card migrated.
Phase-16.step-1: Synchronize AGENTS.md and all six GRACE artifacts with the approved transition state.
Phase-16.step-2: Expose only the focused and real-work ConciseStudentTaskCard target shapes.
Phase-16.step-3: Define the exact twenty-slug compatibility inventory, CardMigrationEvidence, and cutover rejection commands.
Phase-16.step-4: Confirm all twenty current cards remain legacy-compatible and receive no concise PASS in this phase.
Phase-16.step-5: Confirm the implemented catalog remains thirteen pages until Phase 19.
Phase-16.artifact-check-16-1: AGENTS.md, templates/task-template.md, docs/task-validation-policy.md, and the six GRACE XML artifacts contain synchronized target and compatibility facts.
Phase-16.artifact-check-16-2: Baseline scans observe exactly twenty legacy-marker cards and thirteen collection pages.
Phase-16.blocked-when: BLOCKED if the compatibility list differs from the twenty existing slugs, any Phase 17 through 20 outcome is marked implemented, XML is invalid, or the current cards or collections are represented as already cut over.

Phase-17.name: ConciseWaveA
Phase-17.goal: Migrate exactly eight focused cards in Wave A with per-card local deterministic and CardMigrationEvidence PASS.
Phase-17.step-1: Migrate immutable-category-totals, stable-product-sort, loop-closure-bindings, browser-event-loop-order, discriminated-load-state, typed-object-property, response-union-narrowing, and validate-unknown-profile.
Phase-17.step-2: Reject legacy markers, excess hints, open details, invalid metadata, full-document JavaScript, local-link failures, or synchronization drift; record external execution as NOT_RUN.
Phase-17.step-3: Record the focused commit, pushed state, per-card Beads evidence, graph delta, verification delta, and complete wave report.
Phase-17.artifact-check-17-1: Exactly the eight named cards plus their graph, verification, and Beads records change; M-TASK-TEMPLATE remains the governing contract.
Phase-17.artifact-check-17-2: M-CATALOG projections preserve unique thematic and optional interview membership.
Phase-17.blocked-when: BLOCKED if any named card lacks a complete local deterministic verdict, its central action becomes ambiguous, a required local link fails, or shared Markdown, collection, XML, or Beads facts drift.

Phase-18.name: ConciseWaveB
Phase-18.goal: Migrate exactly eight focused browser, DOM, CSS, and accessibility cards in Wave B with per-card local Markdown evidence.
Phase-18.step-1: Migrate this-callback-binding, stale-search-response, delegated-dynamic-list, idempotent-event-listeners, accessible-keyboard-tabs, modal-focus-lifecycle, flex-long-text-overflow, and container-responsive-grid.
Phase-18.step-2: Apply concise structure, minimal-markup, accessibility-wording, manual-check-text, local-link, and synchronization gates without opening an editor or browser.
Phase-18.step-3: Record the focused commit, pushed state, per-card Beads evidence, graph delta, verification delta, and complete wave report.
Phase-18.artifact-check-18-1: Exactly the eight named cards plus their M-CATALOG projections, graph, verification, and Beads records change.
Phase-18.artifact-check-18-2: No CSS or visual behavior is asserted by automated tests; the Markdown-visible requirements, starter, solution, and manual-check wording agree.
Phase-18.blocked-when: BLOCKED if minimal markup cannot preserve the task, any required local context is hidden, the Markdown contract is contradictory, a required local link fails, or synchronization drifts.

Phase-19.name: ConciseWaveCAndCatalogCutover
Phase-19.goal: Migrate four React cards, add users-api-list as the only real-work card, atomically cut over the root to fourteen collections and twenty-one cards, then remove the compatibility exception.
Phase-19.step-1: Migrate react-derived-list, react-batched-counter, react-effect-subscription, and react-strictmode-cleanup, then add concise users-api-list.
Phase-19.step-2: Add collections/real-work/README.md, its one users-api-list entry, the thematic entry, and the root link atomically.
Phase-19.step-3: Run the full twenty-one-card and fourteen-collection cutover commands with compatibility present, remove the exact list only after PASS, then rerun the identical commands without compatibility.
Phase-19.step-4: Synchronize all shared contracts, graph facts, verification facts, Beads evidence, and the focused cutover commit.
Phase-19.artifact-check-19-1: Twenty-one concise cards, fourteen collection pages, five exact metadata rows per card, one thematic membership per card, and one supported users-api-list real-work membership pass.
Phase-19.artifact-check-19-2: M-TASK-TEMPLATE has no legacy shape; the scan passes with compatibility present, M-GOVERNANCE and M-TASK-VALIDATION remove the exception, and the identical scan passes again after removal.
Phase-19.blocked-when: BLOCKED if any local concise scan fails, users-api-list Markdown does not describe all required states or embeds an unresolved external dependency, root and real-work collection cannot change atomically, or compatibility would be removed before all cards pass.

Phase-20.name: ConciseLocalAudit
Phase-20.goal: Audit the local root, all fourteen collections, and all twenty-one cards without inferring final user acceptance.
Phase-20.step-1: Record the complete thirty-six-file inventory, current branch divergence, pushed commit, and remaining risks.
Phase-20.step-2: Confirm closed details, concise order, balanced fences, and details pairing in source Markdown across both task classes.
Phase-20.step-3: Reconcile every local deterministic result with CardMigrationEvidence and Beads facts.
Phase-20.step-4: Inspect all twenty-one source task files.
Phase-20.step-5: Inspect the root and all fourteen source collection files, including the single real-work projection.
Phase-20.artifact-check-20-1: Every local file, title, relative link, details pair, code fence, editor instruction, collection membership, and real-work projection has a recorded deterministic result.
Phase-20.artifact-check-20-2: The top-level story and final acceptance decision remain open for the user.
Phase-20.blocked-when: BLOCKED if any required local file, relative link, Markdown structure, catalog projection, XML/Beads synchronization fact, or branch-divergence result fails.

ExecutionPolicy.controller-owns: docs/development-plan.xml, docs/knowledge-graph.xml, docs/verification-plan.xml, and catalog synchronization decisions
ExecutionPolicy.worker-owns: Only the explicitly accepted task cards, colocated assets, and packet-scoped derived updates
ExecutionPolicy.replan-trigger: Ambiguous metadata, collection, editor instruction, task class, or profile; duplicate learning goal; missing prerequisite or local asset; unnecessary multi-file split; full-document JavaScript wrapper; contradictory card, thematic, interview, or real-work facts; failed local deterministic evidence; or any requirement for new permanent runtime tooling.
ExecutionPolicy.checkpoint-requirement: Every concise redesign step must leave task class, editor profile, preservation ledger, artifacts changed, checks run, both target-editor fields marked NOT_RUN: Markdown-only delivery, local deterministic verdict, thematic/interview/real-work sync, technical status, remaining risk, and next action.
